correctness.rationale: For arbitrary dimensions, sign partitions define a finite union of closed sets of two independently chosen nonnegative rank-at-most-one diagonal rectangles with zero crossed rectangles. Signed factors realize every such member, including degenerate blocks. Frobenius distance attains its minimum on the closed nonempty output set. On each nonnegative block the Eckart--Young lower bound is attained with nonnegative top singular vectors, and independently optimized blocks yield the exact spectral score. For ambient minimum dimension at most two all ranks are either zero, one, or full, while Seraghiti--Vandaele--Gillis give a rank-two nonattainment in three by three. The package checker passed 146 tested reconstructions; finite tests supplement, not replace, the proof. No unproved infinite computational enumeration is invoked.

value.rationale: This is a naturally motivated boundary issue for nonconvex direct ReLU matrix factorization: a recently established rank-two nonattainment contrasts with NP-hard rank-one optimization. The new general closedness theorem settles whether a global rank-one best approximation exists, and a constructive exact combinatorial spectral objective permits direct verification and explicit minimizer recovery. Combining that with the known counterexample establishes the smallest possible rank and ambient dimension where nonattainment can occur. It clarifies that NP-hardness does not entail ill-posedness and is more than a routine reformulation of SVD, because signed rectification creates two independently optimized blocks with a global coupled sign partition. Exponential partition complexity, possible historical overlap, and finite-precision issues are stated limits.
